match.reason: The bank card covers cash versus credit transactions and accounts receivable and payable for businesses in Victoria, not the consumer payment methods (debit, credit, buy now pay later, cash) with their interest, fees and tracking trade-offs that this Stage 5 Commerce point teaches.

draft.title: Pros and cons of payment methods
card: Debit card
Spends money you already have in your bank account. You cannot spend more than your balance, though some accounts allow a small overdraft, so there is no debt to repay.
Credit card
Borrows money from the card provider, which you must repay. If you do not pay the full balance by the due date, interest is usually charged. Late fees may also apply.
Buy now pay later
Lets you take a product now and pay it off in instalments. It borrows money too. Missed payments can bring late fees, and it can tempt people to buy more than they can afford.
Cash
Physical notes and coins. It is easy to track, because you can see what is left in your wallet. It is also easy to lose or have stolen, and it cannot be recovered like a card can.
draft.remember: Debit spends your own money. Credit and buy now pay later borrow it, so costs can be added. Cash is easy to track but easy to lose.

a.q: Which payment method spends money the buyer already has in their bank account?
opts: Debit card
Credit card
Buy now pay later
Credit card with a high limit
a.why: A debit card takes money straight from your own account, so no debt is created. Credit cards and buy now pay later both borrow money that must be repaid, and a higher limit only means more can be borrowed.
a.clue: Which one does not create a debt?

b.q: Jaya buys a $300 jacket with a credit card. She forgets to pay the full balance by the due date. What is the most likely result?
opts: Interest is charged on what she owes
The $300 is taken from her bank account at once
Her cash is lost because the card was not paid
She pays nothing extra because the card is borrowed
b.why: A credit card borrows money, so unpaid balances usually attract interest, and late fees may also apply. The money is not taken from her account straight away, which is how a debit card works.
b.clue: Think about what happens to borrowed money that is not repaid on time.

b.best: Interest is charged on what she owes

problems.detail: The debit card line says some accounts allow a small overdraft, 'so there is no debt to repay'. An overdraft is borrowed money that must be repaid, so the sentence contradicts itself. Either drop the overdraft clause or say there is no debt unless an overdraft is used.

check.summary: The debit card line contradicts itself: it mentions overdrafts but then says there is no debt to repay, and an overdraft is a debt. Both questions and their explanations are otherwise sound.
